value.nature: STATISTICAL -- 'one cannot in general predict the outcome of an individual contact'

source.ref: Malucci & Ruffino, 'Current Rating Power Connectors Using Voltage Drop Criteria' (Molex white paper, content.molex.com, PUBLIC); tests at 17/20 A on 8-contact tin-plated connectors; healthy Ro ~0.8 mOhm (Rms ~0.3); Amphenol GS-12-1031 initial high-power contact resistance <=0.8 mOhm. Context: docs/research/gpu-12vhpwr-fault-phenomenology-2026-06-10.md thread two

notes: THE KEY DEGRADATION NUMBER: thermal-runaway onset when contact voltage drop rises 10-30 mV (32 mV at the 9 A class = ~3.5 mOhm above the ~0.8 mOhm healthy baseline); runaway then proceeds to tin's 0.143 V melting voltage. The threshold's EXPLICITLY STATISTICAL nature is the documented argument for TREND-AND-IMBALANCE detection over any fixed limit (owner slate) -- it grounds both the alarm imbalance trigger (alarm.12vhpwr_per_pin) and the dV/dI requirement (dvdi.requirement_tier_verdict, ~3x margin at 1 mOhm resolution). DERIVATION OPACITY (2026-06-10 panel): the Malucci tests ran at 17/20 A (~2x the 7-9 A rating); the 0.0322 V figure for the 9 A class is the PAPER'S extrapolation whose formula the research doc does not reproduce -- distinguish it from the directly-averaged 0.028 V statistical onset; verify the extrapolation against the white paper at promotion (the 3.5 mOhm conversion and the dV/dI ~3x margin are load-bearing on it).

source.ref: Molex Micro-Fit 3.0 family ('typically 30 cycles'); corroborated by Corsair and Seasonic 12VHPWR guidance. Mechanism: fretting corrosion dominates tin-plated power contacts (Samtec 'The Pain of Fretting Corrosion'; connectorsupplier.com) -- micro-motion fractures brittle tin oxide, fresh metal re-oxidizes, resistance rises, I2R heats, positive feedback. Context: docs/research/gpu-12vhpwr-fault-phenomenology-2026-06-10.md

notes: The pinned cycle-life fact + the fretting mechanism. Field timeline context: documented melting cases run weeks-to-months between install and failure. The inspection-paradox CLAUSE rides as its own H entry (conn.inspection_paradox) citing this fact -- class purity: the pinned number is A, the operational inference is H.

source.ref: Owner slate 2026-06-10, riding the pinned conn.mating_cycle_life fact (~30 cycles) + the fretting mechanism: re-seating a connector to INSPECT it consumes mating-cycle life and accelerates the fretting wear being inspected for. Context: docs/research/gpu-12vhpwr-fault-phenomenology-2026-06-10.md

notes: THE INSPECTION PARADOX: physical inspection of a melt-prone connector is itself a wear event (~30-cycle life, fretting accelerated by re-seating; one documented case was 'inspected every 3 months' and melted anyway). This is the product argument for ELECTRICAL trend monitoring (dV/dI + imbalance) over physical inspection regimes -- CEC watches the connector without touching it. Fixture-less H per ruling D1 (operational inference, no mechanism).

source.ref: Owner slate 2026-06-10 (comparator defaults + hog tightening; slate numbering OQ-58/OQ-59 -- the spec-side home is section 6.13/OQ-57 'lock the threshold default'). Grounds: the 9.2/9.5 A ratings (conn.12vhpwr_pin_ratings), der8auer's 22 A failure capture + Malucci statistics (conn.malucci_runaway_onset, evidence.gpu_transient_measured), and ASUS shipping the same 9.2 A + open-pin trip in Power Detector+ ('one or more 12VHPWR pins exceed 9.2 amps or are at 0 amps'). CEM-EXACT BASIS carries the derivation-class verify note (CEM 5.1 paywalled)

notes: Firmware comparator/alarm defaults, owner-ruled: WARN above 9.5 A sustained per pin; ALARM above 11 A sustained >1 s (tightened from the FEM-probe-era 12 A hog default -- 12 A survives only as an instantaneous ceiling); CRITICAL on imbalance ratio >2.0 or an energized ~0 A lane. Ordering sanity: balanced 600 W = 8.3 A < rating 9.2 <= WARN 9.5 < ALARM 11 << measured failure >=22 (der8auer cable reads ratio >=22/8.5 = 2.6 > 2.0, a LOWER BOUND since the hog reading is a clamp-ceiling floor -- the CRITICAL trigger fires on the documented failure with margin). Industry corroboration: ASUS ships the same per-pin + open-pin posture. SURFACED AMBIGUITY (2026-06-10 panel, OWNER TO RESOLVE at the section-6.13 threshold lock): the ruled 'per-pin current = lane current / 2' does not map cleanly onto the 12VHPWR Standard architecture, which senses each +12V pin DIRECTLY (6 INA240s on 6 per-pin shunts -- no division); EPS carries 4x12V/cable and PCIe 3x12V/cable, so neither gives /2 either. The ruling is encoded VERBATIM; the computation's architecture binding is the open half. SPEC-REVISION CANDIDATE: these defaults land in section 6.13 at promotion (threshold default lock, spec OQ-57).
